message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of the most highly‑rated crime‑thrillers that hit theaters (or streaming platforms) in 2020. These films earned praise for tight plotting, strong performances, and atmospheric tension—making them worth a watch if you’re craving a good whodunnit or a gritty caper.

| # | Title | Release (US/UK) | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|-----------------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | 12 Feb 2020 (US) / 13 Feb 2020 (UK) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological thriller that blends sci‑fi horror with domestic abuse tropes, delivering a tense cat‑and‑mouse chase that keeps viewers on edge. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | 28 Mar 2020 (US) / 29 Mar 2020 (UK) | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Hugh Grant | Ritchie’s signature fast‑paced style shines in this heist‑drama, with witty dialogue and a star‑packed ensemble that turns a simple drug‑deal plot into a layered crime saga. |
| 3 | **The Irishman** | 24 Nov 2020 (US) / 25 Nov 2020 (UK) | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Though it leans toward epic gangster drama, its investigative narrative and use of de‑scalation technology make it a compelling crime‑thriller that spans decades. |
| 4 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | 11 Jun 2020 (US) / 12 Jun 2020 (UK) | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen, Mark Rylance | A courtroom thriller that doubles as a political crime drama, featuring sharp dialogue and a tense build‑up to the historic trial. |
| 5 | **The Hunt** | 20 Oct 2020 (US) / 21 Oct 2020 (UK) | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish crime‑thriller that follows a man’s descent into paranoia after being falsely accused, blending social commentary with suspenseful storytelling. |
| 6 | **The Nightingale** | 18 Dec 2020 (US) / 19 Dec 2020 (UK) | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | A historical crime‑thriller set in colonial Australia, known for its visceral action sequences and a gripping revenge plot. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | 27 Nov 2020 (US) / 28 Nov 2020 (UK) | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned crime‑thriller, praised for its realistic combat scenes and complex character dynamics. |
| 8 | **The Platform** | 15 Jan 2020 (Spain) / 16 Jan 2020 (UK) | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish dystopian thriller that uses a vertical prison setting to explore class conflict, delivering a chilling psychological narrative. |
| 9 | **The Invisible Man** (Netflix) | 12 Feb 2020 (US) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss | (See above – note that it was also available on Netflix, making it accessible for home‑viewers.) |
|10 | **The Last Full Measure** | 23 Jun 2020 (US) | Michael Apted | Tom Hanks, Ben Affleck | A war‑crime thriller that examines the moral complexities of battlefield decisions, featuring strong performances and a tense narrative arc. |

### How to Pick Your Next Watch

- **If you love slick, fast‑moving heists** → *The Gentlemen* or *The Irishman* (for a longer, more epic take).
- **For a psychological edge** → *The Invisible Man* or *The Hunt*.
- **Looking for courtroom drama** → *The Trial of the Chicago 7*.
- **Want something with a historical twist** → *The Last Duel* or *The Nightingale*.
- **Prefer a social‑commentary thriller** → *The Platform* or *The Hunt*.

All of these films received solid reviews on Rotten Tomatoes (above 70% fresh) and have strong IMDb scores (mostly 7+). If you’re looking for a crime‑thriller that’s both entertaining and thought‑provoking, any of the above will do the trick. Happy watching!
